brief: JPMorgan reiterates its Underweight NVDA credit rating after Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, following board moves to remove him over an alleged relationship with a woman tied to Chinese intelligence and a separate alleged relationship with an NVIDIA employee; NVIDIA says it has no reason to believe secrets were compromised. CFO Colette Kress becomes interim CEO while the board weighs external versus internal successors. CDS hit record highs; JPM expects weaker cash spreads and continued spread weakness through the transition and legal fallout. Separately, Commerce reportedly halted a chip-diversion probe into Singapore's Megaspeed after NVIDIA contact (the case moved to DOJ, not dropped); JPM expects tougher oversight once the new, more Democratic Congress sits in January, with risk extending beyond China sales to overseas customers and financing. JPM also flags circularity risk: NVIDIA's balance-sheet support for lower-rated AI counterparties raises its own exposure, and Huang's departure removes a key advocate reassuring lenders on GPU-financing deals, though JPM does not expect hyperscalers to alter near-term plans.
